subject: Technical qualification: auth, routing & output contract
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@streamlytics.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + technical constraints and ask

Hi Neha / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a set of technical questions so we can scope the POC:

Summary: Streamlytics wants to integrate Redwood for a conversational support feature and a later-phase document search reranker. Key constraints:
- Must support our SSO/OIDC flow and be able to integrate with our internal token exchange flow (we don't want raw API keys baked into services).
- We host part of our stack in a VPC and need either Private deployment or a VPC peering option for traffic to the inference endpoints.
- Expected steady-state: ~100 qps across a mix of short chat turns and batch re-ranks (3–5k docs per query). Peak bursts to ~500 qps for short windows.
- Latency target for chat: 200–350ms p50 for single-turn replies (50 tokens avg). For reranking, throughput is more important than <200ms p50.

Tech questions:
1) Auth: Can your SDK support short-lived tokens via our OIDC exchange? Do you support token introspection / audience restriction for tokens issued by our IdP?
2) Routing & topology: If we use Redwood Hosted initially, can requests be pinned to a region and fall back to Dedicated variants? How granular is per-route routing (model level vs per-API-key)?
3) Structured output / tool calling: We want deterministic structured JSON outputs for a set of tools (ticket-create, KB-lookup). How do you recommend enforcing schema and failover if model emits unexpected fields?
4) Embeddings & reranker: Do you recommend computing embeddings client-side and calling a separate rerank endpoint, or doing an internal rerank step within the same completion/chat call? Tradeoffs?
5) Request/response schema: For chat vs completions, how do you recommend setting max_tokens, stop sequences, and streaming parameters to meet our latency targets while avoiding truncation?

I've attached a high-level requirements PDF. Can you send a short tech recap and proposed next steps so we can align with our infra and security teams?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering
Streamlytics

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@streamlytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + technical constraints and ask

Priya —

Great to meet you both earlier. High-level answers inline and proposed next steps at the bottom. I'll also attach a short doc summarizing SDK auth modes for your infra team.

1) Auth: Yes — our SDK supports OIDC flows. We have two recommended patterns:
   - Token-exchange (recommended): your services mint a short-lived internal token after OIDC auth; that token is exchanged with Redwood via our token-exchange endpoint. No long-lived API keys are stored.
   - Managed OIDC integration (Enterprise/Private): we can integrate client-side verification and audience restriction at the Private control plane level if you want Redwood to validate tokens directly.

   We also support token introspection hooks and audience scoping. We'll need a sample IdP token payload to validate the exact claim names you use.

2) Routing & topology:
   - Region pinning is supported at the route (client API key / route) level. Fallbacks are configured per-route and can be at model-variant granularity (e.g., gptx-fast -> gptx-safe).
   - Hosted -> Dedicated fallbacks are supported; we can define failover priorities and latency-based routing.

3) Structured output / tool calling:
   - We suggest defining an explicit output contract (JSON Schema) and using our function/tool-calling primitives so the runtime returns validated JSON when confident.
   - For enforcement, Redwood Optimize can run a lightweight schema-check at inference time and either: 1) reject/mask outputs that don't match, 2) reroute to a validator model, or 3) return raw output plus a validation result. We can map that behavior to your tolerance for failures.

4) Embeddings & rerank:
   - For initial POC, compute embeddings server-side (your backend) and call a separate embeddings endpoint + rerank pipeline. This gives better control and scales independently from chat traffic.
   - We also offer an on-call reranker (internal pipeline) that can be invoked as part of the chat flow for tighter latency but it's more complex to test and tune.

5) Chat vs completions (quick guidance):
   - Chat for multi-turn state and system/user/assistant roles; completions for one-shot structured responses.
   - Set max_tokens to the expected response size + buffer (we typically recommend 1.5x expected tokens to avoid truncation). Use stop sequences for deterministic termination when you control the delimiter.
   - Streaming=true helps reduce time-to-first-byte; for p50 latency targets it's often valuable. You can combine streaming with a small chunk_ms (e.g., 50–100ms) so partial tokens stream quickly.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will send a short tech note on chat/completions and tokenization guidance (code + recommended params).
- We provide a sandbox token for your infra team to run a concrete request/response contract with a small test dataset.
- Security: we'll share the IdP token claim mapping and a short checklist for our Private/VPC options.

Attaching: redwood-sdk-auth-modes.md

Would a technical working session on Thurs 2026-09-09 10:00 PT work for your team?

Best,
Neha Kapoor

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@streamlytics.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + technical constraints and ask

Priya — quick practical notes to help your infra team draft the request/response contract. Replying inline to Neha's points.

Chat vs completions:
- Chat: prefer for multi-turn with context (we keep a rolling message buffer in the runtime). Use chat when you need role-separated history and tool-invocations.
- Completions: simpler single-turn generation; slightly cheaper when you only need one-shot structured output.

Tokenization and max_tokens:
- Tokenization varies by model. For budgeting, calculate using an estimated tokenization multiplier (English prose ~0.75–1.0 tokens/word). For safety, assume 0.8 tokens/word for planning.
- max_tokens should be set to the max expected output tokens + 20–30 token safety buffer. If you need exact truncation semantics, use stop sequences on a stable delimiter (e.g., "
###END###").

Stop sequences & structured output:
- If you require strict JSON objects, use the tool-calling/function schema and schema enforcement. Fallback: append a stop token after the JSON and validate post-hoc in your service.

Streaming semantics & latency tuning:
- Set streaming=true to stream partial tokens. For low p50 latency, adjust chunk_ms (50–150ms) to balance throughput and CPU.
- Continuous batching at the runtime may introduce slight additional latency; use per-route batching knobs to cap batching window when you need strict SLOs.

Embeddings & rerank options:
- Pattern A (recommended for POC): offline embeddings + an approximate nearest neighbor index + an in-service rerank call that fetches top-N and reranks synchronously.
- Pattern B (low-latency): request an internal rerank step inside the chat completion call — lower network hops but harder to scale independently.

Example parameter set we often start with for chat single-turn replies (to hit ~200–350ms p50):
- model: redwood-turbo-1
- streaming: true
- max_tokens: 64
- temperature: 0.0–0.3
- stop: ["
###END###"]
- chunk_ms: 75
- per_route_batch_window_ms: 20 (to limit batching delays)

Example completions call for strict JSON output:
POST /v1/completions
{
  "model": "redwood-suite-struct-v1",
  "prompt": "<your prompt here>
Return JSON with keys: action, args",
  "max_tokens": 200,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "stop": ["
###END###"],
  "stream": false
}

We'll bring a short live demo of the streaming behavior in the Thursday session if that helps.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
